nodes.norm_label: repository as the single source of truth

nodes.norm_label: follow-up limit warns rather than goes quiet

nodes.author: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)
nodes.community_name: ADR-0042 Layered agent guidance and Claude Code hooks as repo tools

nodes.author: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)
nodes.community_name: ADR-0042 Layered agent guidance and Claude Code hooks as repo tools
nodes.rationale: First query fetches only headers of cross-referencing PRs, second fetches comments only for delivery PRs, so strangers cannot set the workload; 2 calls and 2.39 s per tick.

nodes.label: Byte-for-byte old/new output comparison
nodes.author: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)
nodes.rationale: Old and new tools ran on 20 real targets with shrunken pages; caught [bot] suffix and >2^31 IDs as strings; ten negative controls.

nodes.label: Diesel
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: ORM plus typed query builder with schema.rs and SQL migrations; --diff-schema generation since 2.1; built-in PostgreSQL ranges, at_time_zone, union_all, transaction builder.

nodes.label: SeaORM
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: Higher-level entity/relationship ORM with Rust migration crate and entity-first schema sync in 2.0.

nodes.label: SQLx
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: Async SQL toolkit; SQL migrations and optional checked query macros; direct correspondence between reviewed SQL and what runs.

nodes.label: Abstraction ordering SQLx < Diesel < SeaORM
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: Describes everyday APIs not quality; higher abstraction removes plumbing but hides translation; power has several meanings.

nodes.label: Diesel mapping of Calendar's PostgreSQL behaviour
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.norm_label: diesel mapping of calendar's postgresql behaviour
nodes.rationale: Ranges/GiST, time-zone conversion, UNION ALL, read-only snapshot, keyset pagination and roles all have Diesel routes; xmin concurrency and generated columns need explicit care.

nodes.label: Migration execution versus generation
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: Execution applies versioned changes and tracks progress; generation diffs a model to produce the next change. EF gives both; Rust tools differ in where the boundary sits.

nodes.label: Migration-history handover from EF
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: An EF history table does not become a new tool's history; retain EF chain and hand over at a boundary or adopt a reviewed baseline distinguishing fresh from existing databases.

nodes.label: Person-hour estimate for Rust port
nodes.author: Codex (GPT-6)
nodes.rationale: Low-confidence: 60-130 h for the persistence slice, 200-420 h for the complete backend; 12-24 h per option for a representative evaluation slice.

nodes.label: Reading budget and limits disclosed

nodes.label: Incident-to-lasting-change loop
nodes.author: Codex
nodes.rationale: Something goes wrong, evidence is examined, a lesson recorded, guidance or enforcement changes, later work is checked for recurrence; effectiveness still being evaluated.

nodes.label: Limits of the assessment
nodes.author: Codex
nodes.rationale: No evidence of adoption, production reliability, or agent superiority; process cost is high; epic coordination evaluated only in simulation.

nodes.label: Routing lessons to guidance layers
